details:
**Kim Jong-un**
The current supreme leader of North Korea, who took power in 2011 after the death of his father, Kim Jong-il. He is the third generation of the Kim dynasty, which was founded by his grandfather Kim Il-sung.

**Juche**
North Korea's official state ideology, usually translated as "self-reliance." Developed under Kim Il-sung, it stresses political, economic, and military independence and is used to justify the country's isolation and the rule of the Kim family.

**"Hermit Kingdom"**
A nickname for North Korea, one of the most isolated countries in the world. The name was originally used for the Joseon dynasty of Korea, which tried to shut itself off from foreign influence in the 1800s.

**Assassination of Kim Jong-nam**
Kim Jong-un's estranged half-brother was killed with the VX nerve agent at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia in February 2017. North Korean agents convinced two young women, Siti Aisyah of Indonesia and Doan Thi Huong of Vietnam, that they were taking part in a TV prank show when they smeared the poison on his face.

**Sony Pictures hack and The Interview**
In 2014, hackers linked to North Korea broke into Sony Pictures, leaking emails and unreleased films, in retaliation for the comedy The Interview, starring Seth Rogen and James Franco. The film depicts a plot to assassinate Kim Jong-un.

**Lazarus Group**
A state-backed North Korean hacking group blamed for the Sony hack, the 2017 WannaCry ransomware attack, and large thefts of cryptocurrency used to fund the regime.

**Bangladesh Bank heist and the "Shalika Foundation"**
In 2016, hackers tied to the Lazarus Group used the SWIFT banking network to try to steal nearly 1 billion dollars from Bangladesh's central bank account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. About 81 million dollars was stolen, but one transfer to a "Shalika Foundation" in Sri Lanka was stopped after a bank noticed that "Foundation" was misspelled.

**USS Pueblo**
A US Navy intelligence ship seized by North Korea in January 1968. Its crew of 82 was held for 11 months before being released, and the ship is still displayed in Pyongyang as a museum.

**Blue House raid**
In January 1968, commandos from North Korea's Unit 124 infiltrated Seoul in an attempt to assassinate South Korean President Park Chung-hee at the Blue House, the presidential residence. The raid failed, and two days later North Korea seized the USS Pueblo.

**"Balloon war"**
In 2024, North Korea sent hundreds of balloons carrying trash and manure across the border into South Korea, in response to South Korean activists who had sent balloons carrying anti-regime leaflets north.

**Nuclear weapons program**
North Korea carried out its first nuclear test in 2006 and has conducted six in total. It has also tested intercontinental ballistic missiles despite UN sanctions, which led to summits between Kim Jong-un and Donald Trump in 2018 and 2019 that failed to produce a disarmament deal.
